name: Nuclear plant safety
summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on one power line as Russia strikes Ukraine's energy system
state: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has depended on a single off-site line since repairs after an 18-day loss of off-site power, in a ceasefire window the IAEA brokered (Al Jazeera; World Nuclear News). Russian strikes on 3 Nov hit energy sites across Ukraine and left large areas without power (Outlook India). No damage to safety systems has been reported as of 4 Nov.
for_you: No public health action is needed. Follow official national and IAEA updates if travelling to or living near affected regions.
rubric_hit: Plant reliant on a single off-site line amid strikes = Watch; no safety-system damage

sources.title: World Nuclear News — IAEA and Russia discuss Zaporizhzhia situation
Outlook India — Russia attacks Ukraine ahead of Abu Dhabi talks

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
